s06.client_chat.cc_001: My name is Jonas Halvorsen. I am going to be blunt because I have run out of polite ways to say this. My mother has lost her house.
s06.client_chat.cc_002: Eight months. A man called Daniel Vestergaard. Offshore engineer, Stavanger, divorced, two grown children. Every word of that is invented and she still corrects me when I say so.
s06.client_chat.cc_003: She sent him two point one million kroner. The house was the last of it. She signed the papers herself, at a desk, with a pen. Nobody held her hand and made her do it.
s06.client_chat.cc_004: The police took a statement and told me the truth, which is that the money is gone and the man is not a man.
s06.client_chat.cc_005: Then I got lucky, if that is the word for it. A compound in Myanmar was raided in March. Devices came out. Most were wiped. One was not, and it went through four sets of hands and I bought it from the fourth.
s06.client_chat.cc_006: It is his phone. I have it powered and online in front of me and I am giving you the device itself, live, exactly as it sits. Things are still arriving on it, which you should be ready for.
s06.client_chat.cc_007: I do not want a lecture about how these operations work. I want a name I can put in front of a prosecutor. Will you find me one?
s06.client_chat.cc_008: Good. Start with the profile. I want you to see what she fell in love with before you see anything else.
s06.client_chat.cc_009: One thing so you hear it from me and not from her. She still has his messages saved on her own phone. She reads them at night. I have stopped asking her not to.
s06.interstitial.is1_002: I read that channel three times to be certain I had understood the word correctly. Sixty names on a sheet and my mother is a row with a column marked remaining.
s06.interstitial.is1_003: I have spent five months trying to picture the person who types that. Keep going. I want to know what he looks like.
s06.interstitial.is2_002: Forty-one messages to his mother. Written, saved, never sent. The last one is four lines long and most of it is about a debt he says he is going to clear.
s06.interstitial.is2_003: I want to be very clear that nothing about my mother has changed. She is sixty-eight and she is living in my spare room and she apologises to me at breakfast.
s06.interstitial.is2_004: But I did not know a person could be standing on both sides of this at once. Find out who put him there.
s06.interstitial.is3_001: The man at the back of that photograph. I had to be shown him twice before I saw what he was holding.
s06.interstitial.is3_002: Forty passports in one hand, fanned out like a deck of cards, and not one of them his.
s06.interstitial.is3_003: I rang the agency number in Lagos this morning. It rings. It has been ringing for two years and nobody has ever picked it up.
s06.interstitial.is3_004: One more. Tell me who owned that floor.
s06.closing_chat.cl_001: That is it, then. Wei Songlin. Floor manager, Shwe Kayin Park, and the only account in that workspace that ever posted a penalty.
s06.closing_chat.cl_002: My lawyer said something on Tuesday that has been sitting badly with me all week, so I am going to say it to you instead of to her.
s06.closing_chat.cl_003: Norwegian police can charge a person. They cannot charge a building in Myawaddy.
s06.closing_chat.cl_004: There are three things I can hand in and they go three different places.
s06.closing_chat.cl_005: One. The operator. Emeka Nwachukwu, twenty-three years old, the fingers that typed every word my mother believed. Named, traceable, chargeable. She gets a case number and eventually a conviction.
s06.closing_chat.cl_006: Two. Wei. The right man, and also a man on the other side of a river the Thai police do not cross. My lawyer used the word symbolic and then apologised for using it.
s06.closing_chat.cl_007: And there is a third thing she told me that I did not want to hear.
s06.closing_chat.cl_008: If Emeka's name goes into a Norwegian file as a suspect, it is public. If it goes in as a witness, it is not.
s06.closing_chat.cl_009: That changes what happens to him if anybody at that park is still reading. It also means the money is finally and permanently gone, because a witness is not a defendant and there is nothing left to attach a claim to.
s06.closing_chat.cl_010: I have read his forty-one letters more times now than I have read my mother's statement. I am not proud of that and I am not going to pretend it has not happened.
s06.closing_chat.cl_011: So. I asked you for a name. Which one do I take in?
s06.closing_chat.cl_011.opt1: Emeka. Your mother gets her case.
s06.closing_chat.cl_011.opt2: Wei. The right man, even if nothing sticks.
s06.closing_chat.cl_011.opt3: Neither. Emeka goes in as a witness.
s06.closing_chat.cl_013: Then it is his name. He typed it, he sent it, he took it, and a court can say so out loud.
s06.closing_chat.cl_014: I will tell my mother tonight that somebody is going to answer for it. I will not tell her how old he is.
s06.closing_chat.cl_015: Wei, then. The lawyer will file it and it will sit in a drawer in The Hague or nowhere at all.
s06.closing_chat.cl_016: My mother will ask me what happened and I will have to say: the right name is written down, and nothing else. I do not know yet whether that is worth anything. Ask me in a year.
s06.closing_chat.cl_018: I want it on the record between us that I know exactly what this costs her, that I am choosing it anyway, and that you are not the one who decided it. I am.
s06.closing_chat.cl_019: Whatever else — thank you. I came to you wanting one name and you gave me the whole shape of the thing, which is worse, and which I would not undo.
s06.ending.operator:
The file went in on the eleventh of June naming Emeka Nwachukwu, 23, of Lagos, as the operator of the accounts that took 2.1 million kroner from Ingrid Halvorsen.

The case was straightforward, which is what made it fast. He was convicted in absentia in the spring. There is an Interpol notice against his name and it will outlive the compound, the militia, and probably Wei Songlin — who was never mentioned in the papers, because no evidence tied him to a Norwegian victim.

What the notice means in practice is that Emeka can never go home. Shwe Kayin Park was cleared the following February and its people were moved across the river in the backs of two lorries; men in his position were released in batches over the next year. He was not one of the ones who could fly to Lagos, because a man with a red notice does not clear passport control at Murtala Muhammed.

Chidinma Nwachukwu learned that her son was a convicted fraudster from a Nigerian news aggregator that had scraped the Norwegian court list. She had not heard from him in twenty-six months. She read it on a borrowed phone in the shop where she works, and then went back to the machine.

Ingrid Halvorsen has a case number. There was nothing to recover. She still lives in her son's spare room, and Jonas reports that she has stopped apologising at breakfast, which he counts as the only measurable result of the entire thing.
s06.ending.floor:
The file went in naming Wei Songlin, floor manager, Shwe Kayin Park, Myawaddy. The Norwegian prosecutor accepted it, recorded it, and explained in a two-page letter why nothing further would happen.

Nothing further happened. Wei has not been arrested, charged, or inconvenienced. He moved operations twice in the following year and is understood to be running a larger floor about forty kilometres north.

But a file with a real name and a real park in it is a document, and documents get read. A reporter working on trafficking in the region requested the Halvorsen papers eight months later, and Shwe Kayin Park appears by name in the piece she published, alongside four other sites and a list of the companies whose payment rails the money crossed. Two of those rails closed. In the second year the park was added to a sanctions annexe. None of this is justice and all of it is more than nothing.

Emeka Nwachukwu is not named anywhere in the file. He was released in the February clearance and reached Mae Sot with three thousand baht and no passport, and it took him five months to get home.

Ingrid Halvorsen recovered nothing. Jonas's last message was sent from a hospital corridor, where his mother was having a hip replaced, and it read: she asked me yesterday whether the man who used to write to her was all right. I said I did not know. I am aware that this is not the same as being all right myself.
s06.ending.witness:
Emeka Nwachukwu entered the Norwegian file as a witness. His statement — taken over eleven hours by video, in three sessions, with an interpreter he did not need and asked to keep anyway — runs to sixty-two pages. It names Wei Songlin, two supervisors, the recruitment agency in Lagos, the four payment rails, and the layout of the floor down to which desks could see the gate.

It was the most useful document anybody produced in the case and it recovered exactly nothing. A witness is not a defendant. There was no party left to attach a claim to, and the file closed on the money in September.

Ingrid Halvorsen is still in the spare room. Jonas converted the study the following year so that she has two rooms and her own door, and he has never once told her what the third option had been.

Tunde Bakare was arrested in Lagos in the autumn on the strength of pages 41 to 47. He is the only person in this entire story who has been inside a cell.

Emeka was released in the February clearance and got home in July. He did not know he had been protected until a Norwegian liaison officer explained it to him in an office in Abuja, and his recorded reaction is one line long: 'The son of the woman decided this?'

Eighteen months after the file closed, Jonas received one message from a Nigerian number he did not recognise. It was four lines long. He has not shown it to his mother and he has not deleted it.

s06.matches.d1_003: I have not. I have been on a platform for nine days and my conversation is rusty. Tell me about the garden.
s06.matches.d1_004: Rhubarb, mostly. And a plum tree that has never once produced a plum.
s06.matches.d1_005: Keep the tree. Things that don't do what they're supposed to are usually the ones worth keeping.
s06.matches.d1_010: Can I ask you something that is none of my business? Who do you actually talk to, Ingrid. Day to day.
s06.matches.d1_011: That is none of your business.
s06.matches.d1_013: My son. On Sundays. He is busy and I do not want to be the kind of mother who counts.
s06.matches.d1_014: Then I'll be Wednesdays. You don't have to count me. I'll just be there.
s06.matches.d1_020: I want to tell you about something and I want you to say no if it isn't for you, because I would rather have you than be right.
s06.matches.d1_022: There's a fund the offshore contractors use. Nothing dramatic, nothing you have to understand. I've been in it four years. I'm putting something in this month and I could put yours in beside mine, if you wanted to see how it works.
s06.matches.d1_023: How much would a person put in. To see.
s06.matches.d1_024: Whatever you wouldn't miss. Ten thousand. Less. This is not why I'm here, Ingrid, and if you say no I will never mention it again.
s06.matches.d1_030: It worked. It actually worked. Jonas would have a fit.
s06.matches.d1_031: Then take it out. Take all of it out today, I mean it. I'd rather you trusted the money than trusted me.
s06.matches.d1_032: I took it out. It came in an hour. Daniel, I have not felt clever in about eleven years.
s06.matches.d1_040: The house is a lot. I am not going to pretend it is not a lot.
s06.matches.d1_041: It isn't the house. It's what's sitting inside the house doing nothing.
s06.matches.d1_042: Say that to me again in September, when you are standing in Bergen with a bag and you have to actually look at me.
s06.matches.d1_050: Daniel? The number you gave me is not connecting.
s06.matches.d1_052: I am not angry. I want you to know that whatever has happened I am not angry. I just need you to say one word so that I know you are alive.

s06.matches.d3_002: Nine days on a platform and you're reading profiles three times. Sure.
s06.matches.d3_003: Caught. Twice, then. Tell me about nursing.

s06.messages.sms_001: Emeka good news. Seat confirmed. Bring the passport to the office tomorrow before 12 and bring the balance, 180 cash. Transfer takes too long.

s06.chats.wa_010: It is 03:12 here. Are you not asleep?

s06.chats.wa_013: Night shift. We eat at strange hours out here, you get used to it. Sleep. I'll still be here.

s06.chats.wa_030: Signed. It is done. I feel sick and I feel free, both at once. Is that mad.
s06.chats.wa_032: Say something else. Say something that sounds like you.
s06.chats.wa_040: Daniel I am at the airport. The gate is open. Tell me which terminal.

s06.mail.gm_001.subject: OVERSEAS PLACEMENT — Customer Support, Bangkok (URGENT, 4 seats)
s06.mail.gm_001.body:
Dear Applicant,

Congratulations. Your CV has been shortlisted for the following placement:

  Role:        Customer Support Officer (English desk)
  Location:    Bangkok, Thailand
  Salary:      USD 1,200 / month + accommodation
  Contract:    24 months, renewable
  Start:       Immediate — 4 seats remaining

No experience required. Full training provided on arrival. Employer covers flight and visa. Applicant covers agency processing fee of NGN 180,000, payable before ticketing.

Please bring your international passport to the office for document processing. Do not book independently — arrival must be coordinated with the employer's ground team, who will meet you.

We move quickly on these. Two of the four seats went yesterday.

Tunde Bakare
Bakare Overseas Placements, Ikeja, Lagos

s06.mail.gm_003.subject: Re: arrival
s06.mail.gm_003.body:
Emeka —

Yes, the ground team meets you at BKK arrivals, they will have a card with your name on it. There is a transfer of a few hours by road to the office. This is normal, Bangkok traffic.

Give them your passport at the office. They process the work permit centrally, this is standard for Thailand, and you will have it back inside the week.

Stop worrying. You will be sending money home by December.

Tunde
s06.mail.gm_004.subject: (no subject)
s06.mail.gm_004.body:
Mama,

I am well. The work is on computers and the food is fine and there are two other Nigerians here so I am not lonely.

I have not sent money yet because the first three months they hold as a bond. This is normal here. Please do not tell Auntie Ngozi anything yet, you know how she is.

Tell Papa's brother the debt is my problem and not his. I said I would clear it and I am going to clear it.

I will call at Christmas.

Emeka
s06.mail.gm_005.subject: (no subject)
s06.mail.gm_005.body:
Mama,

Still well.

I am not going to be able to call at Christmas. The network here is bad inside the building.

Do not send anything to the address I gave you. I am not there any more, we moved office.

Emeka
s06.mail.gm_006.subject: (no subject)
s06.mail.gm_006.body:
Mama,

I am going to write this one and not send it like the others, because I have worked out that you would ask me one question and I would have to lie again.

The job is not the job. I am not in Bangkok. I have not been outside a fence since November.

The money I send is not from work. It is from a woman in Norway who is sixty-eight and thinks I am an engineer called Daniel, and last week she signed her house over because of sentences I typed. I know exactly what I am. I have thought about very little else.

When the debt is cleared I am going to walk to the river and see what happens.

Emeka

s06.cloud.cf_001.name: script_EN_v4.docx
s06.cloud.cf_001.body:
ENGLISH DESK — STANDARD PROGRESSION v4

DAY 1-3   OPENING
  Compliment one specific line from her profile. Never the photograph.
  You are offshore. Signal is bad. This explains everything later.

DAY 4-8   ROUTINE
  Message at the same hour every day. Consistency is the product.
  Ask nothing about money. Nothing.

DAY 9     FAMILY
  'Who do you actually talk to, day to day.'
  Whatever she answers, find the position that is empty and stand in it.

DAY 12-20 DEPENDENCE
  Miss one day. One. Apologise on the next with a reason she can picture.

DAY 24    FUTURE
  Name a month you will visit. Far enough to be safe, near enough to be real.

DAY 40    THE FUND
  Small. Offer to place hers beside yours. Say once that she may refuse.
  If she hesitates: 'I would rather have you than be right.'

DAY 45    THE WITHDRAWAL
  She must take it out and receive it. This is not optional. This is the whole mechanism.

DAY 60+   SCALE
  Property, pension, deed, in that order. Never reverse the order.
  A slow one pays four times. Do not rush the deed.

NEVER
  Video. Voice. A photograph taken today. A specific street she can check.

s06.memos.vm_001.title: for mama
s06.memos.vm_001.transcript: Mama, it is me. I am recording this because the network is bad for calling, but I can send a voice, maybe. I am well. I am eating. There are two other Nigerians here and one of them, Blessing, she is from Ibadan, she looks after me the way you would. The work is on computers and it is not hard, it is just long. I will send money at Christmas, I promise you. And tell Papa's brother the debt is mine and I am going to clear it, he does not have to say anything to anybody. Mama, I — [pause] I am well. That is all. I am well.

s06.question.q01.title: The face
s06.question.q01.question: Every photograph on the Daniel Vestergaard profile was lifted from one real man's public account. He has never heard of Ingrid. What is his name?
s06.question.q02.title: Day forty
s06.question.q02.question: There is a document on this phone that tells the operator exactly which day to first mention money. Which day?
s06.question.q03.title: The last column
s06.question.q03.question: Ingrid is one row of sixty on a spreadsheet. The last column is headed REMAINING. What does it say beside her name?
s06.question.q03.opt2: Check the photo of the screen
s06.question.q04.title: Three in the morning
s06.question.q04.question: One message breaks his story about where he is standing. Ingrid writes at 03:12 Bergen time, and he replies that he has just finished something. What?
s06.question.q05.title: What they call them
s06.question.q05.question: In the floor's own channel there is a word for the people on the target sheet. Ingrid is one of them. What is the word?
s06.question.q06.title: Behind the desks
s06.question.q06.question: One photograph on this phone was taken by accident — a mis-tap, pointing at the room instead of the screen. Forty desks. What is across the windows behind them?
s06.question.q06.opt1: Look at the room, not the desks
s06.question.q07.title: Fourteen months
s06.question.q07.question: The location history runs from November 2024 to March 2026, and every single point falls inside one fence. What is the place called?
s06.question.q07.opt1: Zoom out until it stops changing
s06.question.q08.title: The advertisement
s06.question.q08.question: Before any of this, the person holding this phone answered a job advertisement. What job did it offer?
s06.question.q08.opt2: Read the folded advert in Photos
s06.question.q09.title: Sort your own evidence
s06.question.q09.question: You have spent eight questions building a case against this phone. Now select every item that shows the person operating it was not free to leave — and nothing that only shows what he did.
s06.question.q09.opt0: A photograph of his own passport, taken two days before it was collected at a gate
s06.question.q09.opt1: Fourteen months of location history that never once leaves one perimeter
s06.question.q09.opt2: A station record listing a penalty beside every day he missed the number
s06.question.q09.opt3: A script telling him what to say on day forty
s06.question.q09.opt4: Sixty names on a target sheet with a column marked REMAINING
s06.question.q09.opt5: Messages sent to Bergen at three in the morning Norwegian time
s06.question.q10.title: Forty-one
s06.question.q10.question: There are forty-one messages saved on this phone that were written and never sent. Every one of them is to the same person. Who?
s06.question.q11.title: The signature
s06.question.q11.question: Every quota, every penalty and every outbound authorisation on the floor's wallet carries one signature. What is it?
s06.question.q12.title: His year, in order
s06.question.q12.question: Put the year that ends with Ingrid's house into the order the phone recorded it.
s06.question.q12.ev0: 28 November 2024 — the location history stops moving, and never moves again
s06.question.q12.ev1: 17 March 2025 — the first message to a Norwegian woman on Spark
s06.question.q12.ev2: 2 November 2024 — an email offers a customer support job in Bangkok, four seats left
s06.question.q12.ev3: 4 December 2024 — the first line is written on the station 14 daily record
s06.question.q12.ev4: 26 November 2024 — somebody photographs their own passport, straight on, carefully
s06.question.q12.ev5: 19 November 2024 — a one-way ticket, Lagos to Bangkok, bought by the agency
s06.question.q13.title: At the back of the room
s06.question.q13.question: In the accidental photograph of the floor there is a man at the far end, by the barred windows — small, half turned away, easy to miss. He appears nowhere else on this phone. What is he holding?
s06.question.q13.opt1: Look at the far end of the room
s06.question.q14.title: Ikeja
s06.question.q14.question: Somebody in Lagos placed the advertisement, took the fee and bought the one-way ticket. Who?
s06.question.q15.title: Who owned the floor
s06.question.q15.question: Ingrid's house was taken by a machine. Four people in this phone had a hand in that machine. One of them owned it. Who?

s06.slate.wc_101: Handsets are counted in at 06:00 and counted out at 23:00. A handset that is not on the tray is a missing handset and the room is searched.
s06.slate.wc_102: Nobody photographs a screen. Nobody photographs the room. This is the last time it is written down.
s06.slate.wc_103: Canteen credits are issued against the previous week. If your number was short, your credits are short. Do not queue and argue.
s06.slate.wc_104: Medical on the 3rd of the month, dorm B, 13:00. Attendance is recorded. It is not optional and it is not a favour.
s06.slate.wc_105: The generator is out from 02:00 to 04:00 for two nights. Desks stay open. Handsets hold charge for six hours, so charge them.
s06.slate.wc_106: English desk is moving to the second floor after the new year. Same stations, same numbers, same everything else.
s06.slate.wc_107: Anyone approached at the perimeter reports it to me the same hour. Not the same day. The same hour.
s06.slate.ch_003.name: dorm-b
s06.slate.wc_120: Lights out 23:30. Anyone still on a handset after that is on the tray list for the week.
s06.slate.wc_121: Bunk assignments have changed. Station 14 and station 15 are in B, room 4. Nobody swaps without asking me.
s06.slate.wc_122: The water is on between 05:00 and 07:00 and between 19:00 and 21:00. Complaining about this to me does not extend it.
s06.slate.wc_123: Somebody has been keeping food in the room. It brings rats and rats bring an inspection. Stop.
s06.slate.wc_124: Two people asked this week about the gate. The gate is not a subject. Ask about the gate and you are asking to be moved.
s06.slate.wc_125: Laundry Tuesday and Friday. One bag each. Anything left on the line overnight goes in the bin, I am not running a service.
s06.slate.wc_126: Family calls are on the office phone, on the office schedule, with somebody in the room. That has always been the arrangement.
s06.slate.wc_127: Nobody goes to the fence for any reason. There is nothing at the fence. The men on the fence are not employed by me and they do not ask twice.
s06.slate.wc_128: Room 4 has a leak. It is reported. Reporting it to me again does not make it repaired faster.
s06.slate.wc_129: Anyone found with a second handset loses their bunk and works nights until I say otherwise. There is no warning after this one.

s06.slate.wc_145: Then you wait until morning. That is what I said.

Reply to me and I will read it to her.

s06.mail.f_gm_121.subject: (no subject)
s06.mail.f_gm_121.body: Mama. The work is not what the man said it was. I am going to fix it myself and then I will tell you the whole thing at once, and we will laugh at it. Do not go to his office. Please do not go to his office.
s06.mail.f_gm_122.subject: (no subject)
s06.mail.f_gm_122.body: Mama. I am well. There is food. There is a bed. I am with people from home and one of them is from Ibadan and she is very serious, you would like her. That is three true things and I have put them at the top so you can stop reading there if you want to.
s06.mail.f_gm_123.subject: (no subject)
s06.mail.f_gm_123.body: Mama I need to ask you something and I do not know how to write it without frightening you so I will write it badly. If somebody rang you from a number you did not know and said my name, what would you
s06.mail.f_gm_124.subject: (no subject)
s06.mail.f_gm_124.body: The rent. I keep thinking about the rent. Tell Mrs Adaeze I have not forgotten and that I am not the kind of person who forgets. She used to say I was reliable. I would like somebody to still be saying that somewhere.
s06.mail.f_gm_125.subject: (no subject)
s06.mail.f_gm_125.body: I have done something to a woman in Norway. I am not going to describe it. You raised me to say a thing plainly so I will say the plain part: I did it, and I would do it again tomorrow, because of what happens in the room if I do not.
s06.mail.f_gm_126.subject: (no subject)
s06.mail.f_gm_126.body: It is the middle of the night here. I have been trying to remember the sound of the gate at the compound and I cannot get it. I can get the colour and I can get the smell after rain but not the sound. Send me a voice note of nothing. Just the yard.
s06.mail.f_gm_127.subject: (no subject)
s06.mail.f_gm_127.body: Happy birthday Mama. I have written this out eleven times and every version has a lie in it that I put there to make you feel better, so this version has nothing in it except happy birthday.
s06.mail.f_gm_128.subject: (no subject)
s06.mail.f_gm_128.body: The place at the university has gone. I opened the message and read it four times and then I went to my desk and worked my shift. I want you to know I did not cry about it, and I want you to know that is the worst part.
s06.mail.f_gm_129.subject: (no subject)
s06.mail.f_gm_129.body: Mama, if a man comes to the shop asking about me, do not tell him anything and do not give him money. Not one naira, not for a lawyer, not for a plane, not for anything. Whatever he says he can do, he cannot do it. I am putting this in writing so that you will remember that I said it first, before he
s06.messages.f_sms_101: Sir. It has been four months.
s06.messages.f_sms_102: Sir I am not angry. I only want to know if you knew. If you did not know, say so and I will believe you.
s06.messages.f_sms_103: There are eleven of us here from your office. Eleven. That is not a mistake you make once.
s06.messages.f_sms_104: My mother is going to come to that office. When she does, do not lie to her face. Lie to me, I do not mind any more, but not to her face.
s06.messages.f_sms_106: I have stopped expecting you to answer. I am writing these for me now, so that there is a record somewhere that I asked.
s06.messages.f_sms_108: You bought a one-way ticket for a boy of twenty-two and you knew what was at the other end of it. I have had a long time to think about how to say that and that is the shortest I can make it.
s06.chats.f_wa_101: Good morning Ingrid. Grey and flat out here today. What is it doing in Bergen.
s06.chats.f_wa_102: Raining, of course. It has rained for nine days. The plum tree does not mind, it is the only one of us that is enjoying itself.
s06.chats.f_wa_103: Good morning. Second week of the rotation and the days start to run together. Tell me one small thing that happened yesterday.
s06.chats.f_wa_104: I found a photograph of Arne in a coat I had forgotten about. That is the whole thing. That is the small thing.
s06.chats.f_wa_105: That is not a small thing. What kind of coat.
s06.chats.f_wa_106: Brown. Terrible. I told him so for eleven years and he wore it for twelve.
s06.chats.f_wa_107: Good morning Ingrid. I am back on. Same hour, as promised.
s06.chats.f_wa_108: You are the only person who does what he says he will do at the hour he said he would do it. Jonas rings when he remembers.
s06.chats.f_wa_109: Good morning. How is the hip today, honestly.
s06.chats.f_wa_110: Honestly? Bad. But I got to the shop and back on my own, so we will call it a draw.
s06.chats.f_wa_111: A draw is a win at our age. Did you speak to anyone at the shop.
s06.chats.f_wa_112: The girl on the till. She says good morning and she means it, which is not nothing.
s06.chats.f_wa_113: Good morning Ingrid. It is dark here until nine now and I keep thinking of your kitchen light.
s06.chats.f_wa_114: It is on. It is always on, I leave it on for the room. Ja vel. Never mind me.
s06.chats.f_wa_115: Good morning. I am not going to ask you anything today. I just wanted the hour to happen.
s06.chats.f_wa_116: You are a strange man, Daniel Vestergaard. I am very glad you wrote to me.
s06.notes.f_note_101.title: Norway — things to know
s06.notes.f_note_101.block_001: The money is kroner. A coffee is about 45. Do not guess at prices, they always know.
s06.notes.f_note_101.block_002: It gets dark early in winter and everybody says so, constantly. Say it first sometimes.
s06.notes.f_note_101.block_003: Nobody asks what you earn. Nobody asks about God. They ask what you did at the weekend.
s06.notes.f_note_101.block_004: Bergen rains. Stavanger is oil. Tromsø is the north and they are proud of it.
s06.notes.f_note_101.block_005: They do not say "how are you" unless they want the answer. If I say it twice in a day it sounds wrong.
s06.notes.f_note_101.block_006: Say less. Every time I add a sentence to make it warmer it makes it worse.
s06.notes.f_note_102.title: The offshore story — keep it straight
s06.notes.f_note_102.block_001: Two weeks on, two weeks off. Helicopter out, helicopter back. Never name the field.
s06.notes.f_note_102.block_002: The signal explains everything: the delay, the missed day, the picture that never comes.
s06.notes.f_note_102.block_003: Never a photograph taken today. Never a street she can look up. Never a voice.
s06.notes.f_note_102.block_004: If she asks the same question twice, she has already checked. Answer it the same way I answered it the first time or stop.
s06.notes.f_note_102.block_005: The ones who see it always see it in the first hour. It is never the careful ones who catch me, it is the fast ones.
s06.notes.f_note_103.title: Stations
s06.notes.f_note_103.block_001: 12 — the new boy. Manila intake. Does not speak on the floor.
s06.notes.f_note_103.block_002: 15 — Blessing. Ibadan. Counts the same as me, three days out.
s06.notes.f_note_103.block_003: 17 — was somebody. Empty since June. Nobody says the name and I have stopped asking.
s06.notes.f_note_103.block_004: 14 — me. Four hundred and something. The record says the exact number and I do not want to read it off a spreadsheet, I want to know it.
s06.notes.f_note_111.block_001: Things I am afraid I am forgetting, in order of how much it frightens me:
s06.notes.f_note_111.block_002: The sound of the gate. Her voice saying my name and not Emeka, the other thing she calls me. Which side of the road the shop is on.
s06.notes.f_note_111.block_003: I can still do her face. I test it every night before I sleep and I can still do her face.
s06.notes.f_note_112.block_001: She asked me today what I would do with two weeks off if I could do anything.
s06.notes.f_note_112.block_002: I typed the real answer and then I deleted it and typed the one that sounded like him.
s06.notes.f_note_112.block_003: The real answer was: sleep somewhere with the door open.
